subject: AWS private offer — Acme pricing & marketplace revenue-share alignment
messages:
From: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@amazon.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni, laura_bennett
Cc: Jordan Marks <j.marks@acme.com>; Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer for Acme — draft attached

Hi Vivek / Laura,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. Attached is the draft private offer for Acme Corp. Highlights: 20% list discount off our marketplace price, 6% marketplace rev-share to Redwood, 1-year term with automatic renewal, and standard AWS Marketplace terms.

Acme asked for an expedited turnaround so they can close before their fiscal quarter end. If Redwood is comfortable with the rev-share and the term alignment, I can push this into the private offer workflow on my side and initiate the DocuSign packet.

Attachments: Acme_AWS_PrivateOffer_v1.pdf (PDF - draft private offer)

Thanks,
Priya
AWS Marketplace — Strategic Accounts
priya.sethi@amazon.com

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer for Acme — draft attached

Laura / Markus / Rachel — looping you in. Key asks from Acme and AWS: 20% off list, AWS is allocating a 6% rev-share to Redwood, and a 1-year auto-renew term. Acme procurement is asking us to accept AWS standard termination and data residency clauses (no custom SLAs).

Questions for Deal Desk / Legal:
- Is 6% rev-share within our standard marketplace threshold for a deal this size (ARR ~$1.2M initial)?
- Any objections to the auto-renew + no-custom-SLA language?
- If we need to counter, what is the maximum discount/rev-share we can accept without Exec OK?

I've attached a quick pricing comparison (pricing_breakdown.xlsx) and highlighted the margin impact. If legal is comfortable, I recommend we approve the private offer subject to Exec sign-off on any rev-share >7% or contract term changes.

Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer for Acme — draft attached

Team — I reviewed the draft. High-level legal flags:
- The private offer uses AWS's standard indemnity and limitation of liability clauses that effectively push risk to Redwood if we accept customer-side claims via the marketplace. We typically ask for carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct.
- Auto-renew without a renewal pricing review is risky; suggest we require a 30-day renewal notice and a mid-term pricing review for first renewal.
- Rev-share at 6% is acceptable commercially, but combined with a 20% discount we need to ensure we meet our floor margin. See attached redline (Redline_PrivateOffer_v2.pdf).

Propose: Approve the private offer subject to: (a) Redwood's acceptance of 6% rev-share max without C-level approval; (b) change auto-renew to "auto-renew with 30-day pricing review"; (c) include explicit carve-out language for gross negligence. If AWS cannot accept the small redlines, we escalate to Evelyn for executive sign-off.

-Markus
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redline_PrivateOffer_v2.pdf (PDF - redlined private offer)

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@amazon.com>; Jordan Marks <j.marks@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer for Acme — draft attached

Quick commercial note: Acme has signaled urgency and is sensitive to price — they will churn to competitors if this slips. From a revenue perspective, the deal is strategic (platform play into their analytics product). 20% off + 6% rev-share over 1 year leaves us borderline but acceptable if we hold the renewal review. My recommendation: accept Markus's conditional approvals and ask AWS to incorporate the three redlines. We should also set an internal cap: any revision that moves rev-share above 7% or extends term beyond 12 months requires Evelyn's sign-off.

If Markus's redlines are non-starters with AWS, we escalate to Evelyn with the margin impact and customer risk summary.

Laura
Head of Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private offer for Acme — draft attached

Thanks all for the summary and redline. I reviewed the margin impact in pricing_breakdown.xlsx and the legal redlines. Given the strategic value and the risk of losing Acme, I approve the proposed path:

- Approve the private offer with 6% rev-share and the 20% list discount for a 12-month term.
- Require AWS to accept the three redlines: 30-day renewal/pricing review, gross negligence carve-out, and explicit limitation of liability cap preserved.
- Internal rule: any increase that pushes rev-share >7% or extends the term >12 months must come back to me.

Vivek — please instruct Priya to proceed with the DocuSign packet once AWS confirms they can accept the redline items. Loop me on the HubSpot deal (HS-2739) and attach final DocuSign link.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Revenue & Operations
Redwood Inference
